bundle.author: emilybgoodpartyorg
bundle.title: perf(elections): overlap the fetch groups a cold location or profile render waits on
bundle.body:
## Why

Emily reported that voter guide pages load slowly when arriving from the location search and sometimes when opening a candidate profile. Measured on production on 2026-10-09: a cold city page takes 1.6 to 3.2 s to first byte, a cold county page 2.3 to 2.8 s, a cold profile 0.8 to 1.3 s, and any warm page about 0.15 s. Cold is the common case for two reasons: there are about 20,000 city pages, so most arrivals from search land on one nobody opened in the last hour, and Vercel's page cache is per deployment, so every release makes every programmatic page cold again (only the 51 state pages are prebuilt).

A cold render fans out to roughly a hundred election-api requests, so its time is the length of the longest chain of dependent reads. The chains on these pages did not overlap: a location route resolved its place lists, then its own date refresh, then the overlapping county and state offices with their date refresh, then the featured-people chain (places, dates, up to 48 candidacy reads six at a time, persons, published profiles, product photos), then two serial Sanity reads for the template. None of those groups needs the one before it.

## What changes

- Location routes start the featured-people chain (the longest on the page) as soon as the page is known to render, resolve their own dates alongside the overlapping-office read, and the renderer resolves the Sanity template while the people finish.
- The featured-people loader starts the officeholder and removal reads before the per-tier date refresh instead of after it.
- The profile loader starts nearby officials as soon as the office's geo id is known and other candidates as soon as the position id is, with the removal set started first and joined inside each loader. The profile route resolves its view once per request instead of once for metadata and once for the page, and preloads its template.
- The overlapping-offices read goes through `getElectionsPagePlace`, so the state and county rows share one cached entry with the featured-people block instead of being requested again in a narrower column set (two fewer election-api reads per cold city page, one per county page).
- The position renderer loads officeholders, nearby offices and the guide title together.

Every page renders the same content from the same data; only the order the reads start in changes. Nothing is trimmed, no budget changes, and no concurrency limit changes. One small cost: the global template is now read even when a custom template wins, which is one extra cached Sanity CDN read on that path.

`docs/elections.md` gains a section on what a cold render costs and the rules that keep the fetch groups parallel, including why `<Suspense>` streaming would not shorten a cold ISR render here.

## What to eyeball on the preview

A county, a city and a profile page should look identical to dev. I am diffing the visible text of the same URLs on dev and the preview and timing cold preview renders before marking this ready.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches high-traffic ISR routes and many concurrent election-api/Sanity reads; behavior is intended to be identical but early-started promises and ordering changes increase the blast radius if a new rejecting fetch is added without the documented `.catch` pattern.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Cold ISR renders on elections location and people pages were serialized; this PR overlaps independent fetch chains so time-to-first-byte tracks the longest dependency chain instead of the sum of steps.**
> 
> State, county, and city routes call **`startFeaturedPeople`** (featured carousel + Sanity template preload) as soon as the page will render, then **`Promise.all`** their own race date refresh with **`buildOverlappingOfficeItems`**. **`renderElectionsIndexPage`** awaits featured people and **`resolveElectionTemplate`** together. Overlapping offices now read places via **`getElectionsPagePlace`** so state/county rows share the same cached shape as the featured-people block (fewer duplicate election-api reads).
> 
> **`getFeaturedPeople`** kicks off officeholder and removal-list fetches before per-tier date work. **`loadPersonProfile`** starts the removal set first, then nearby officials once `geoId` is known and other candidates once `positionId` is known; the profile route wraps **`resolveView`** in React **`cache`** and calls **`preloadElectionTemplate`**. Position pages load officeholders, nearby offices, and guide title in parallel. **`docs/elections.md`** documents cold-render cost and the parallel-fetch rules (including why Suspense does not help cold ISR here).
> 
> Rendered content and budgets are unchanged; custom-template paths may do one extra cached global Sanity read when a custom template wins.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 81ed5824ac90664f9aa456b03279fb0ded89697f. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

priorFindings.body:
**Unhandled-rejection window on `featuredPeoplePromise`.** This promise is created here but only awaited inside `renderElectionsIndexPage`, after several serial `await`s (the `Promise.all` on lines 48–56, then `resolvePlaceRaceElectionDates` on line 111). If `getFeaturedPeople` rejects in that window — e.g. a network error in `getElectionsPagePlace`, `getCandidacies`, `getPersonsByIds`, or `resolveProductAvatars`, none of which are try/catch-wrapped inside `getFeaturedPeople` — Node.js fires an `unhandledRejection` event that can crash the process.

The PR's own `docs/elections.md` rule says: *"A promise started early must not reject while nothing is listening… `void promise.catch(() => undefined)` right after creating one marks it handled."* This guard is applied to `officeholdersPromise` and `removedPersonIdsPromise` inside `getFeaturedPeople` (lines 272–273) and to `nearbyOfficialsPromise`/`otherCandidatesPromise` in `loadPersonProfile`, but not here.

Falsification check: `getFeaturedPeople` contains multiple bare `await` calls (`Promise.all(tiers.map(resolveTierPlace))`, `resolvePlaceRaceElectionDates`, `mapConcurrently`/`getCandidacies`, `getPersonsByIds`, `resolveProductAvatars`) with no surrounding try/catch, so the comment's "never rejects" claim is not enforced by code.

**Same unhandled-rejection window.** `featuredPeoplePromise` is created here but only awaited inside `renderElectionsIndexPage` after the `Promise.all` on lines 112–115 completes. Same bare-`await` paths inside `getFeaturedPeople` apply.

Falsification check: identical to the state route — `getFeaturedPeople` does not enforce its "never rejects" claim with try/catch.

**Same unhandled-rejection window (district branch).** `districtFeaturedPeoplePromise` is created here and only joined after the `Promise.all` on lines 105–108 and subsequent synchronous work. Same risk as the state and county routes.

Falsification check: same bare `await` calls inside `getFeaturedPeople` with no try/catch.

**Same unhandled-rejection window (city branch).** `featuredPeoplePromise` is created here and only joined inside `renderElectionsIndexPage` after `resolvePlaceRaceElectionDates` and `buildOverlappingOfficeItems` complete (lines 217–220). Same risk as the other routes.

Falsification check: same bare `await` calls inside `getFeaturedPeople` with no try/catch.

output.summary: This PR reorders independent fetch chains on elections location routes (state, county, city/district) and the people profile route so they overlap instead of running serially, reducing cold ISR time-to-first-byte. The key mechanism is `startFeaturedPeople`, which wraps `getFeaturedPeople` in `Promise.allSettled` so the route can hold the result across its own awaits without an unhandled-rejection window — this directly addresses the four prior findings, all of which are now resolved. The overlapping-offices read now goes through `getElectionsPagePlace` to share cached entries with the featured-people block, the profile route deduplicates `resolveView` with React `cache` and preloads its Sanity template, and the position renderer parallelizes officeholders/nearby-offices/guide-title. The scout flagged a forward const reference in `electionTemplates.ts`, redundant token passing in the index-page renderer, and an indirect catch chain on `removedPersonIdsPromise` in `peopleProfile.ts`; all three are non-blocking (the const reference is safe at runtime, the tokens are a harmless fallback, and the catch suppression works through the outer promise catches with the invariant documented in comments). The human reviewer should confirm on the preview that county, city, and profile pages render identically to dev, and that cold render times have improved as expected.
